evidence.excerpt: Amount intended to be collected by this PaymentIntent. A positive integer representing how much to charge in the [smallest currency unit](https://docs.stripe.com/currencies#zero-decimal) (e.g., 100 cents to charge $1.00 or 100 to charge ¥100, a zero-decimal currency). The minimum amount is $0.50 US or [equivalent in charge currency](https://docs.stripe.com/currencies#minimum-and-maximum-charge-amounts). The amount value supports up to eight digits (e.g., a value of 99999999 for a USD charge of $999,999.99).

evidence_boundaries: The OpenAPI spec is Stripe's published contract, not Stripe's server implementation.
The SDKs are outbound clients: their methods map to API operations but are not Stripe server handlers.
stripe-mock serves spec-driven, hardcoded responses (stateless; no response control); it is not Stripe production behavior.
accept-a-payment is an official sample application showing integration patterns; it is not a Stripe customer or Stripe source.
No source in this lock gives access to Stripe's production server implementation; provider source discovery for Stripe is reported as unavailable.
label: authentic pinned public Stripe OpenAPI contract (unmodified); public contract discovery, not Stripe production source
provider_note: Stripe is the API provider whose public contract is analyzed. Stripe is not a Shockwave customer and has not endorsed Shockwave.

provider_source_access.statement: provider source access: unavailable (Stripe's server implementation is not accessible; SDKs, stripe-mock and samples are not provider source)

reconciliation_note: Every operation is not_compared: no Stripe server source was scanned (it is unavailable), so documented operations are neither confirmed nor contradicted by an implementation.

selected_versions.rationale: One coherent combination: the pinned public OpenAPI spec, stripe-python 16.0.0 and stripe-node 23.0.0 all target Stripe API version 2026-09-30.endive (spec info.version, stripe/_api_version.py, src/apiVersion.ts). The consumer templates pin these SDK versions and send Stripe-Version 2026-09-30.endive. accept-a-payment pins the older API version 2023-10-16 and older SDKs, so it is used only as an integration-pattern reference, never as a contract snapshot to compare against.
selected_versions.stripe_mock: Not used. Its README states responses are hardcoded and stateless, and specific responses cannot be requested; its embedded payment_intent fixture has amount 1099. It cannot return the old/proposed response pair, so the demo uses a focused local fixture server configured through the SDKs' supported base-URL options.
selected_versions.version_mismatch: The sample pins Stripe API version 2023-10-16 (apiVersion in server.js; stripe.api_version in server.py) with stripe ^20.2.0 (Node) and stripe==14.2.0 (Python). The demo templates use 2026-09-30.endive with stripe-node 23.0.0 and stripe-python 16.0.0, so the sample is not compared against the pinned contract snapshot. Its Payment Element servers expose merchant routes (GET /, GET /config, GET /create-payment-intent, POST /webhook); /create-payment-intent calls PaymentIntent create, not retrieve. These are merchant routes, not Stripe API operations.
